answer: Lantern-window arrival spacing. Each identity must send its first N transactions with inter-arrival gaps matching an exponentially distributed baseline; a dune of bursty sybil traffic is flagged because synthetic identities emit near-uniform or synchronized timing. An agent must hold and pace traffic across many epochs to mimic organic arrivals, costing real wall-clock latency and idle capacity per identity. Juniper-policy permits throttling flagged clusters to one transaction per window.
